title: Review: usenet-ipfs-smtp 5-commit series
description: Deep pre-merge review of commits 83aa070..79b735c (smtp receive daemon, SPF/DKIM/DMARC/ARC auth, List-ID routing, NNTP client, Sieve delivery, Sieve admin HTTP API)
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — four P0 bugs, two of which (unbounded read_line, ESMTP param parsing) will fire in normal operation with any real MTA sending to this server. The STARTTLS advertisement bug will silently break delivery from MTAs that enforce STARTTLS-policy. The command timeout absence is a DoS surface. Do not merge without fixing at minimum ryw.1, ryw.2, ryw.3, ryw.4.

Confidence: 20% chance of one more missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) usenet_ipfs_sieve::evaluate API is opaque — I don't know if it can return duplicate Keep actions or what happens with a script that has no matching actions (implicit Keep? implicit Discard?). (2) The mail_auth crate behavior under mock_resolve in tests hides real DNS behavior. (3) The Sieve reject multi-recipient race: if two recipients are processed concurrently (not the case here, but if the Sieve eval is async), there could be a TOCTOU on the reject scan. Would raise confidence by: reading the usenet_ipfs_sieve crate source to verify evaluate() semantics, and running the test suite with a real MTA (postfix/exim) sending SIZE-parameterized MAIL FROM.
